key_insight: Behavioral INR learns a shared implicit function for policies from unlabeled episodes, using an episode latent to infer policy identity without supervision.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to model heterogeneous behavior streams in robotics, games, and autonomous systems when policy labels are missing and episode lengths vary.
method: Represents a policy as a state-to-action implicit neural function rather than a coordinate-to-pixel map.
Uses an episode-level latent with FiLM modulation to generate a prior over policies and recover policy identity.
Naturally handles variable-length episodes and different sampling densities across trajectories.
evidence_signal: The method is evaluated on synthetic Gaussian random fields, controlled MuJoCo OOD splits, and real datasets including chess, Formula 1 racing, robotics, and Seek-Avoid, with strongest gains in difficult continuous state-action settings.
watch_item: Performance can be limited when policy identity is already easy to infer from symbolic repetition or low-dimensional action statistics, where amortized history encoders remain competitive.
paper_title: Implicit Neural Representations of Individual Behavior
